List the unsupported features of a SAS program

Source: R/check.R
sas_check.Rd

sas_check() answers one question: which features does this program use that sasonr does not implement? It walks the program as sas_translate() does (the macro processor runs, each step is parsed, analysed and translated, and the variables a step creates are passed on to the steps that follow) without running any step. A step that uses a feature sasonr does not support is reported and the walk goes on with the next step, so one call lists all of them, where sas_run() stops at the first one.

Usage

sas_check(code, work = list())

Arguments

code

SAS source code.

work

Named list of input data frames available as WORK data sets.

Value

A tibble of class sasonr_check, one row per finding: step (the index of the step in the program), line and col (its place in the program, NA when unknown), severity ("error": an unsupported feature; "info": checked when the program runs), feature (what is not supported) and message (the full condition message).

Details

A step whose text depends on a macro variable that only a run sets (CALL SYMPUT, CALL SYMPUTX or INTO : in an earlier step) is not guessed: it is reported with severity "info" and checked when the program runs.

What sas_check() does not tell you:

  • Syntax errors are not reported. They are part of the program, and sas_run() writes them to the log when the program runs.

  • Some refusals depend on the data and appear only when the program runs: a value outside the supported domain of a function, a summary over rows whose order is not known, a date difference that spans years in a basis that is not implemented, for example. sas_run() still stops at those.

Passing sas_check() therefore does not mean that the program will run.

Examples

chk <- sas_check("
data a; x = 1; run;
proc rank data=a out=b; var x; run;
")
chk
#> This program uses 1 unsupported feature:
#> - PROC RANK (line 3)
chk$feature
#> [1] "PROC RANK"
